rationale:
Evidence: the iteration-0 design raced in 60 development trials and never finished. Every run ended off_track, with progress 0.10 to 0.15 and max_error about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit. Steering oscillation was low (0.08 to 0.15), so the robot is not jittering. It drifts steadily away from the line, which points to too little steering authority or response at about 1.6 m/s. Line loss happened 1 to 2 times per run, which fits 8 mm sensor footprints spanning only +/-2 cm: the outer sensors often see no tape on bends. The iteration-1 design never raced, so it gives no evidence either way.

Changes: (1) Geometry: seven sensors spanning +/-3 cm at 1 cm spacing, with 12 mm footprints. Adjacent footprints overlap and cover the 25 mm tape, so the line stays under the array on sharper bends. The sensors sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle for more look-ahead. Chassis dimensions are unchanged so the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m. (2) Controller: sensor weights [-2, -1.33, -0.67, 0, 0.67, 1.33, 2] keep the signal in +/-2 and close to line offset in cm. kp rises from 3 to 5 for more steering authority. kd rises from 0.15 to 0.3 to damp the higher gain. base_speed goes to 1.4, not the 1.2 in iteration 1. At 1.2 the base PWM (about 0.6 of full) probably cannot cover the course in 3 s, and a run that never finishes scores no completion bonus. 1.4 is a compromise between line-keeping and finishing time. ki stays at 0.02 to avoid windup. line_loss stays last_direction.

Expected result: fewer line_loss_events, max_error well below 0.06 m, and a first completion on oval or s-bend. Hypotheses: (a) the drift is under-steering on bends, so kp 5 should cut max_error; (b) the line loss comes from sensor coverage, so 7 wide sensors should drive line_loss_events toward 0. Measurements to check next: completion and completion_time (is 1.4 fast enough?), progress and max_error (where does it leave the line?), line_loss_events (coverage), and steering_oscillation (is kd damping or lagging?).
